content: The intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, such as cobicistat and darunavir: 1. Cobicistat and Infigratinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 2. Itraconazole and Cobicistat: Itraconazole increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative drug. 3. Cobicistat and Ivosidenib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the inhibitor is discontinued, wait for at least five half-lives before resuming the recommended 500 mg daily dose. 4. Darunavir and Ivosidenib: Darunavir increases ivosidenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, follow the same dose adjustment protocol as above. 5. Cobicistat and Ixabepilone: Cobicistat increases ixabepilone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Ketoconazole and Darunavir: Both drugs increase each other's effects by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole with darunavir are not available. 7. Cobicistat and Lapatinib: Cobicistat increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lapatinib dose to 500 mg daily and increase to the indicated dose once cobicistat is discontinued. 8. Darunavir and Larotrectinib: Darunavir increases larotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Cobicistat and Lefamulin: Cobicistat increases lefamulin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 10. Darunavir and Lemborexant: Darunavir increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Cobicistat and Lenolisib: Cobicistat increases lenolisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Levonorgestrel and Darunavir: Darunavir may alter estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a non-hormonal contraceptive method. 13. Cobicistat and Lomitapide: Cobicistat increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Darunavir and Midazolam (oral): Darunavir significantly increases midazolam levels, leading to prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Cobicistat and Osimertinib: Cobicistat increases osimertinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Darunavir and Palbociclib: Darunavir increases palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg daily if unavoidable. 17. Cobicistat and Pomalidomide: Cobicistat increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Darunavir and Red Yeast Rice: Darunavir increases the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis due to its effect on CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 19. Cobicistat and Progesterone (various forms): Cobicistat increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Darunavir and Quetiapine: Darunavir increases quetiapine levels, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose if co-administration is necessary. 21. Cobicistat and Ribociclib: Cobicistat increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Darunavir and Rifampin: Rifampin significantly decreases darunavir levels, leading to reduced therapeutic efficacy.
